proof.text: Compute epsilon d on a basis pair: the two summands are 1 and -1, so epsilon d_0 = 0.

Prove d_p d_(p+1) = 0 by induction on p, checking on basis tuples x. Write x = Fin.cons (x 0) (Fin.tail x), so [x] = h[y] with y = Fin.tail x and prefix s = x 0. Apply d_p to d_(p+1) h[y] + h d_p[y] = [y]. For p=0, apply the degree-zero homotopy identity to d_0[y] and use epsilon d_0=0; it gives d_0 h d_0[y] = d_0[y]. For p=q+1, apply the homotopy identity one degree lower to d_(q+1)[y]; the induction hypothesis kills d_q d_(q+1)[y], so again d_(q+1) h d_(q+1)[y] = d_(q+1)[y]. In either case cancellation gives d_p d_(p+1)[x] = 0.
If S is empty, any tuple of positive length would give an element x 0 of S. Its type is therefore empty, and Finsupp on that type is subsingleton.
